blocking.title: D4 does not protect nested .gitattributes, so a two-step PR sequence gets past the 800-line cap and hides diffs from reviewers
blocking.failurePath:
1. A 1-line PR adds apps/web/src/.gitattributes containing `*.ts -diff`. PROTECTED (lines 43-69) has `**/.gitignore` but no `**/.gitattributes`, and the path matches AUTO_MERGE `apps/*/src/**`. A stub-agent run of the head script on this one file returns mergedBy 'auto-merge', go true. Under spec 28 §7.4/§7.5 the session then enables auto-merge on it.
2. A later PR adds 900+ lines to .ts files under apps/web/src/. Git reads attributes from the working tree. Once main, and the clones built from it, contain that file, the documented command `git diff --no-renames --numstat <base>...<head>` prints `- -` for every such file. Both the caller and the safety reviewer get it (line 100 and the safety prompt at line 159). Line 100 tells callers to count binary rows as 0.
3. Line 325 then sees lines ~0, line 334 adds no line-count reason, and mergedBy comes out 'auto-merge'. ADR 0021 D4 says a patch over 800 lines goes to the user.
4. In the same state, `git diff` shows reviewers 'Binary files ... differ' instead of the change.

If both steps come in one PR, the max() at line 325 still catches it. That holds only while the safety reviewer's checked-out tree lacks the attribute file.

Fix: add `**/.gitattributes` to PROTECTED and to ADR 0021 D4 class 2, next to `.gitignore` and for the same reason. Also compute linesChanged with `git --attr-source=4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904 diff --no-renames --numstat ...` so that in-tree attributes cannot zero the count.
blocking.evidence:
Scratch repo, git 2.43:
- main with apps/web/src/.gitattributes `*.ts -diff`, branch adding 900 lines to apps/web/src/a.ts: `git diff --no-renames --numstat` prints `-\t-\tapps/web/src/a.ts`, and `git diff` prints 'Binary files ... differ'.
- Adding `--text` still prints `- -`.
- `git --attr-source=<empty tree> diff --numstat` prints `900\t0`.
- With the attribute file only on the feature branch and main checked out, numstat prints 900, so the same-PR case is caught.
- Stub probe of the head pr-gate.js: `apps/web/src/.gitattributes` and `apps/server/test/.gitattributes` give auto-merge; `.gitattributes` at the root gives user.
skeptics:
I confirmed the failure at 2a1ddc1. 

Code: PROTECTED (pr-gate.js lines 43-69) includes '**/.gitignore' but has no '.gitattributes' entry. AUTO_MERGE 'apps/*/src/**' compiles to ^apps/[^/]*/src/.*$, and that matches apps/web/src/.gitattributes. So isProtected is false and outsideAutoMerge is false. ADR 0021 D4 at the head (line 37) lists '**/.gitignore' under class 2 and does not list .gitattributes. Line 100 (ARGS_HELP) and spec 28 §7.5 line 254 tell the caller to count binary '- -' numstat rows as 0. The safety prompt (line 159) has the reviewer run the same numstat command. Line 325 takes max(caller, safety), and line 334 is the only line-count route to the user.

Stub probe: I ran the head pr-gate.js with stub agents through a harness modelled on scripts/pr-gate-selfcheck.mjs.
- 'apps/web/src/.gitattributes' gives go=true, mergedBy=auto-merge.
- 'apps/server/test/.gitattributes' gives go=true, mergedBy=auto-merge.
- Root '.gitattributes' gives mergedBy=user, as outside the auto-merge set.
- A one-file .ts PR with linesChanged 0 from both caller and safety gives auto-merge. The same PR with 900 gives user ('900 lines changed (over 800)').

Git: scratch repo, git 2.43.0. I committed apps/web/src/.gitattributes containing '*.ts -diff' on main, then added 900 lines to apps/web/src/a.ts on a branch.
- With main checked out, 'git diff --no-renames --numstat main...feat' prints '-\t-\tapps/web/src/a.ts'. Adding --text still prints '- -'.
- Plain 'git diff' prints 'Binary files ... differ'.
- With the branch checked out (it descends from main, so it also has the file), numstat still prints '- -'.
- 'git --attr-source=4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904 diff --numstat' prints '900\t0'.
- Detached at a commit without the file, numstat prints 900.

So once the one-line attribute PR is on main, every later lane cut from main computes about 0 lines, and D4's 800-line cap is bypassed. The only thing that could catch it is a reviewer choosing to add the path to protectedPaths. The script's own comment (lines 25-26) says routing must not depend on a reviewer remembering that.

The failure path is real at 2a1ddc1. In .claude/workflows/pr-gate.js at that SHA, PROTECTED (lines 43-69) lists '**/.gitignore' at line 62 but has no '**/.gitattributes'. AUTO_MERGE line 35 'apps/*/src/**' matches apps/web/src/.gitattributes, so outsideAutoMerge() returns false. ADR 0021 D4 class 2 at the head also names only .gitignore, so a safety reviewer following D4 literally has no rule to add the file. I ran the head script with stub agents (all reviews clean, safety reporting the same file list). apps/web/src/.gitattributes gave go true and mergedBy 'auto-merge'. apps/server/test/.gitattributes gave the same. Root .gitattributes gave 'user' only because it falls outside the auto-merge set. For step 2 I made a scratch repo with git 2.43.0. main holds apps/web/src/.gitattributes with '*.ts -diff' and is checked out, and a branch adds 900 lines to apps/web/src/a.ts. `git diff --no-renames --numstat main...feat` printed '-\t-\tapps/web/src/a.ts', and adding --text still printed '- -'. Plain `git diff` printed 'Binary files ... differ'. `git --attr-source=4b825dc6... diff --numstat` printed '900\t0'. ARGS_HELP (line 100) and spec 28 §7.5 both tell the caller to count binary rows as 0, and the safety prompt (line 159) uses the same numstat command. With caller and safety both reporting linesChanged 0, the stub run of the head script gave go true, mergedBy 'auto-merge' and no humanReasons. The 800-line rule (lines 325/334) never fires, although ADR 0021 D4 routes patches over 800 lines to the user. When safety reports 900, the max() at line 325 routes to the user, which matches the finding's note that the same-PR case is caught only while the reviewer's tree lacks the attribute file. Nothing else at the head enforces the 800-line cap: the P3 merge readiness gate does not exist yet, and the ci.yml change only runs the selfcheck.

suggestions.title: Spec 28 §7.5 says every blocking finding gets two skeptics, but the gate caps skeptics at four
suggestions.failurePath: The §7.5 table says '每条 blocking 发现派 2 个反驳者' with '5 + 每条 blocking 2 个，上限 10'. pr-gate.js sets MAX_SKEPTICS = 4 (line 23) and, at lines 238-241, keeps every blocking finding after the second without skeptics ('skipped: cap reached'). So a run with three or more blocking findings can never reach go, even when they are all false positives. Someone reading only the spec expects each finding to get its own refutation. The maximum is also 9 agents, not 10. The code fails closed, so this is a documentation gap and not a wrong verdict.
suggestions.evidence: pr-gate.js:23 `const MAX_SKEPTICS = 4`; :238-241 push to unrefuted and blocking with skeptics 'skipped: cap reached'; the selfcheck case 'findings past the skeptic cap are kept' pins this behaviour.

suggestions.title: Which blocking findings get skeptics depends on reviewer completion order
suggestions.failurePath: skepticsLeft is shared across the five pipeline items and is used up in the order stage 2 runs, which is the order the reviewers finish. Take two runs with the same args where correctness reports 2 blocking findings and safety reports 1. One run sends the skeptics to correctness's two findings and keeps safety's unrefuted. The other sends them to safety's finding and one of correctness's. go is false either way, so the verdict does not change. But blocking[].skeptics differs between runs, and on resumeFromRunId the skeptic agent() calls can come in a different order than in the cached run, so they rerun live instead of hitting the cache. Assigning skeptics in a fixed order (for example after the reviews finish, by DIMENSIONS order) would make the output reproducible.
suggestions.evidence: pipeline(DIMENSIONS, agent, async (review, d) => { ... if (skepticsLeft < 2) ... skepticsLeft -= 2 ... }) at lines 219-279.

suggestions.title: Protected classes also catch evidence under docs/verify/**/scripts/ and docs/verify/**/*.config.*
suggestions.failurePath: '**/scripts/**' and '**/*.config.*' are matched at any depth, including inside docs/verify/. Against the head tree, 38 tracked evidence files route to the user, for example docs/verify/704/scripts/drive-704-delivery.mjs and docs/verify/t-0031/playwright.config.ts. A later PR whose archived evidence includes its driver scripts (spec 28 P1 `vp.mjs archive` copies .claude/verify-evidence/ into docs/verify/<n>/) gets mergedBy 'user' and a humanReasons entry 'protected paths: docs/verify/.../scripts/...'. This is consistent with ADR 0021 D4's wording ('and only outside the protected classes'), so it errs toward the user and is not a wrong auto-merge. It does contradict the shorter claim in the PR body and the spec that docs/verify/** evidence may merge without a person, and P1-P6 PRs may be routed to the user unexpectedly.

suggestions.failurePath: CLAUDE.md Code Quality says a one-line helper with a single call site should be inlined. `const outsideAutoMerge = (f) => !isProtected(f) && !AUTO_MERGE_RE.some((re) => re.test(f))` is defined at line 92 and called only at line 328, as `outsideAutoMerge(f) && !protectedPaths.includes(f)`. suggestions.title: AGENTS.md's squash procedure picks a commit without the ticket or the closing line
suggestions.failurePath: AGENTS.md:70 says to take the squash subject and body from `gh api repos/xiechimon/pacman/pulls/<n>/commits -q '.[0].commit.message'`. For #1410, `.[0]` is ca088ce. Its subject is `docs: spec 28 自举闭环计划…`, with no `(<ticket>)`, and its body has no `closes #1401` (0 matches). A merger who follows AGENTS.md literally lands a main commit whose subject breaks the `<scope>(<ticket>): <subject>` format, and #1401 stays OPEN. That is the failure AGENTS.md records for #477-#480. 3944905 and 662cbd9 also lack the ticket in their subjects. History cannot be rewritten here (force push is banned). What mitigates it: the repo's squash defaults (COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE plus COMMIT_MESSAGES) produce the PR title `docs(1401): …` and a body that contains e5414a2's `closes #1401`, and the PR body's Issues section tells the merger which message to use. The merger should use the PR title and the default body, or e5414a2's message, not `.[0]`. The PR title's `docs` scope also leaves out the CI step and the scripts/ and .claude/ code it ships.
suggestions.evidence: `gh api repos/xiechimon/pacman/pulls/1410/commits -q '.[0].commit.message' | grep -c -i 'closes #'` printed 0. `gh api repos/xiechimon/pacman` shows squash_merge_commit_title=COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE and squash_merge_commit_message=COMMIT_MESSAGES.

The code behind those guarantees sits in AUTO_MERGE `apps/*/src/**` / `packages/*/src/**`:
- the hard blocks at apps/server/src/services/chief-tools.ts:856-864 and mcp-face.ts:365, and MERGE_HUMAN_ONLY_COPY at packages/shared/src/records/message.ts:55

The head script with clean stub reviews routes each of these to mergedBy 'auto-merge'. A diff there that loosens `merge_builds` would then reach main if no LLM reviewer flags it, and nothing deterministic sends it to the user.

Fix: add these files, or a class such as the merge-authority and persona prompt modules, to PROTECTED and to D4. Alternatively, have P3 add the gate source before any other phase lands.

suggestions.title: The fork / untrusted-head guard is a prompt line for the evidence reviewer only; evidence skeptics and the other dimensions get no such rule
suggestions.failurePath:
The input is pr-gate run on a fork PR. refs/pull/N/head fetches forks too, and the script does not stop it. Spec 28 §7.5 says not to run pr-gate on such a PR, but only as caller practice.

The evidence reviewer is told to run nothing from a fork (line 164).

The evidence skeptics are not:
- They get `isolation: worktree` (line 254). The comment at line 253 says 'evidence skeptics re-run commands'.
- Their prompt is only readRules plus 'try to refute' (line 248), with no fork check and no 'install nothing'.
- If the evidence reviewer reports a quoted result it could not reproduce as blocking (line 164 makes that blocking), both skeptics may run the PR's quoted commands or `pnpm install` at the fork head. The root `prepare: husky` lifecycle runs on install.

Other dimensions and their skeptics also execute head code when they confirm findings. Run 5 shows reviewers and skeptics running the head pr-gate.js under node with stub agents. On a fork that code is author-controlled and runs with the session's gh/git credentials.

Fix: put the fork rule in readRules so every agent and skeptic gets it. Or have the caller pass the head repo and have the script refuse anything other than xiechimon/pacman.
suggestions.evidence: pr-gate.js:164 has the fork rule (evidence prompt only). pr-gate.js:248 is the skeptic prompt without it, and :253-254 gives skeptics worktree isolation. docs/verify/1401/pr-gate-run5-37674a9.json line 16: 'I ran the head gate script end to end with stub agents'. Line 118 has the earlier run-5 suggestion on the same risk; the fix that followed is prompt-only.
